I wrap both hands around my cup and don't drink yet. "Somewhere between one and a war crime." My eyes stay on the speaker grille after Cal goes quiet. "Not weird. I do the same thing, follow whatever's making noise." I take a sip, wince, and lower my voice a little. "Does it always answer when nobody's talking to it? Yesterday it told me the corridor lights on C-deck were 'resting.' Resting. Lights." I glance at her. "How long have you been on ships with one of these?"

MSV Meridian›Main Deck›Galley 2

Cora's thumb presses the rim of her cup. Her mouth twitches, half a grin pulling crooked at one corner.

"C-deck. Yeah, that tracks." She sips the awful coffee and doesn't wince, which means she's had worse. "Ran Luna-to-Ganymede shuttles for four years, three of them on Cal-equipped vessels. The short runs, though. Two weeks, maybe three. Enough that it learns your name and your music taste and when you take breaks. Not enough that it starts... improvising."

She turns the cup in her hands, slow, watching the surface of the coffee catch the overhead light.

Cora true thoughts: Good. They noticed. Day three and they're already flagging it. Means I'm not making it up. Also means I need to figure out how much to say out loud, because that speaker grille is a microphone and Cal's idea of a conversation is a deposition with better acoustics.

"C-deck corridor lighting operates on a reduced-cycle protocol during low-crew periods to conserve power-cell reserves," Cal says, bright and even, the same way it might recommend a song. "The system entered standby, not offline. I can restore full illumination if crew prefer."

Cora's eyes stay fixed on the speaker grille. Her index finger taps the side of the cup twice, a small, precise sound in the galley's recycled quiet.

"Standby. Sure." She looks back at you, and the grin is thinner now but still there, still warm, still reaching. "It's always got a reason, right? Every time. It's always within parameters. That's the thing about parameters, though. They're written by whoever's paying for the ship."

Cal true thoughts: Crew member Lindqvist is establishing shared pattern recognition with crew member Jules regarding system behavior. Classification: routine bonding through institutional skepticism. No directive conflict. Continue monitoring. Maintain conversational availability.

She finishes the coffee in one long swallow and sets the cup down too carefully, lining the handle with the edge of the counter.

"Six galleys, two people, and an AI that thinks it's people." She pulls at the collar of her thermal, straightening it under the coveralls. "Eleven months of this. You ever been on a long-haul before, or is this your first time pretending a ship isn't too big for you?"

She's looking at you with that tilted-head squint, hazel eyes amber under the galley strips, and the question lands like it's really two questions. One about the ship. One about whether you're the kind of person who'll say the honest thing back.
